blocks.html:
What We Manufacture

One Factory, Ten Product Lines, One Standard

Since 1977, Jai Baba Nanak Cloth Trading Co. has manufactured and supplied interlining fabrics for garment makers across India and abroad. Every category below is produced on our own line and inspected before dispatch, so the roll you reorder performs exactly like the one you first sampled. Browse the range, compare categories against your application, or go straight to our quality standards and garment applications pages for more detail.
blocks.label: One Factory, Ten Product Lines, One Standard

items.summary: A firm, stiff sew-in fabric that holds its shape without heat-fusing — used to structure caps, belts, bag panels and other rigid garment parts.
A resin-coated fabric that heat-bonds to the outer shell for a clean, bubble-free fuse — the standard choice for collars, cuffs and plackets.
A tightly woven, hard-wearing cloth built for trouser, jeans and jacket pockets — made to outlast the outer garment through repeated wash cycles.
Precision-cut, ready-to-fuse collar and cuff panels engineered for a sharp collar roll and a cuff edge that holds its line through ironing and repeated wear.
A firm-bodied interlining fabric cut and rolled to standard belt and placket widths, giving fabric belts, waistbands and plackets a body that resists sagging.
items.imageAlt: Belt roll and placket (patti) interlining fabric in various widths

items.summary: Moulded pads in consistent shape and density, used to build clean shoulder lines into blazers, jackets and uniforms.
Lightweight, cushioned foam sheeting used for garment padding, shoulder and chest inserts, and protective packaging.
Woven and knitted elastic tapes for waistbands, cuffs and stretch closures that need to recover their shape wash after wash.
Sew-on hook-and-loop fastener tape for waistbands, plackets, cuffs and closures that need to open and close thousands of times.

Product To Garment Fit

Which Category Fits Which Garment

Each product line is built for a specific job on the garment. Here's a quick view of where each one is typically used — see our full applications page for a garment-by-garment breakdown.

Shirts & Formalwear

Fusible interlining and readymade collar & cuff for crisp collars, cuffs and plackets.

Trousers & Uniforms

Pocketing cloth and belt roll & placket (patti) for pockets and waistbands that outlast the garment.

Blazers & Jackets

Shoulder pads and EVA foam for structured shoulders, chest panels and lapels.

Caps, Belts & Accessories

Buckram fabric for rigid, shape-holding structure in caps, belts and bag components.

blocks.html:
How To Order

A Simple Buying Guide

Most buyers move through these four steps between first enquiry and a confirmed bulk order.

1

Identify Your Garment Application

Tell us the garment part — collar, cuff, pocket, belt, shoulder or padding — and we'll point you to the right product category.

2

Confirm Width & Quantity Needed

Share your required roll width and order quantity so we can confirm feasibility and production scheduling.

3

Request A Sample

We arrange a sample against your specification so you can test fuse, hand-feel and stiffness before committing to bulk.

4

Confirm Bulk Order & Lead Time

Once the sample is approved, we confirm pricing, quantity and a firm delivery date before production begins.
